title: Cloud platform selection
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's dive into the cloud infrastructure discussion. I've been looking into AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Azure Kubernetes Service, and Google Cloud Platform.

SRE: Hang on, I've noticed some performance issues with Azure during peak traffic. The latency can be quite inconsistent.

Finance Partner: I've crunched some numbers regarding the initial costs. Google Cloud Platform has high data egress charges, which might not be feasible for us in the long run.

CTO: Fair points, everyone. So, we're considering AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Azure Kubernetes Service, and leaving Google out for now, given its high data costs.

SRE: I think we should consider the ease of maintenance and development as well.

Platform Engineering Lead: That's where AWS shines. Their Elastic Beanstalk has a simpler configuration and maintenance.

SRE: Agreed. But we shouldn't overlook the potential benefits of Kubernetes on Azure in terms of containerization and scalability.

CTO: Let's not jump the gun. We should do a cost-benefit analysis of running Kubernetes on Azure before we fully commit.

Platform Engineering Lead: Good call, CTO. In that case, I propose we adopt AWS for our cloud infrastructure, but with a provisional agreement to reevaluate the cost-benefit of using Kubernetes on Azure.

Finance Partner: Sounds like a solid plan to me. I'll prepare the cost-benefit analysis for Kubernetes on Azure.

SRE: I'll look into the performance issues on Azure and see if we can mitigate them.

CTO: Alright, it's settled then. AWS for now, with a proviso for Kubernetes on Azure. I'll sign off on this decision.

Platform Engineering Lead: Excellent. SRE, you'll be owning the AWS implementation.

(Off-topic exchange)

SRE: By the way, CTO, have you seen that new sci-fi series on Netflix? I heard it's pretty good.

CTO: Haven't had the chance yet, but I'll definitely check it out! Back to work...

SRE: Alright, back to work. AWS here we come!

Title: Cloud Infrastructure Decision - AWS Adoption Pending Cost-Benefit Analysis

Following the meeting, the decision was made to adopt Amazon Web Services (AWS) for cloud infrastructure, with the caveat of a cost-benefit analysis for the implementation of Kubernetes on Microsoft Azure. This evaluation is necessary due to the potential long-term benefits of Kubernetes on Azure, such as lower costs for containerization and scalability.

The proposed team will focus on Service Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices throughout this transition.

It is important to note that certain discussions pertaining to specific platforms or concerns were held, but they are not to be included in this record.
